budget.cancellation: terminate, then kill and reap a timed-out validator; roll back a transaction before re-raising process control

determinism.identity: every artifact and report identity is SHA-256 over its exact canonical byte domain
determinism.ordering: manifest order and validator declaration order are preserved while set-like references and conflicts are sorted
determinism.reports: reports exclude clocks, host paths, random values, process IDs, and machine identity
determinism.serialization: UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, compact stable separators, finite numbers, and exactly one trailing newline

effects.filesystem: propose and accept may atomically write only declared contract, report, manifest, and transaction-journal paths; pre-screen and verify are read-only except an explicitly requested report output
effects.mutation: accepted and proposed artifact bytes are never rewritten; revisions require a new versioned ID and supersession edge
effects.process: validators run as direct bounded Python child processes with stdin closed and captured output

ensures: Propose validates the closed schema and writes one canonical immutable proposal plus its proposed manifest record in a single recoverable transaction.
Pre-screen is deterministic, verifies canonical bytes, internal consistency, supersession, active-target uniqueness, manifest binding, and validator references, and explicitly grants no acceptance.
Accept recomputes the pre-screen, rejects stale or forged evidence, copies the exact proposal bytes to the accepted namespace, records authority, and transitions the manifest atomically.

Verify reproduces a self-identifying canonical report for every selected artifact, checks supersession and proposal separation globally, and statically binds active implementations to exact callable signatures and accepted hashes.
Validator execution distinguishes not_run, delegated_recursive, passed, failed, and timeout states without invoking a shell.
Recover either restores every pre-transaction artifact or completes cleanup after a committed transaction; no partial manifest transition is reported as success.

epistemics.accepted: exact pre-screened bytes were transitioned under the named authority
epistemics.bound: the unique callable signature and top-level metadata match the accepted identity
epistemics.invalid: any stale, partial, ambiguous, tampered, unsupported, or contradictory state
epistemics.not_implemented: accepted future intent has no bindable implementation and is never represented as bound
epistemics.prescreened: deterministic mechanical checks passed but intent acceptance was not granted
epistemics.proposed: schema-valid canonical intent registered separately from acceptance

invariants: Unknown and missing fields, duplicate JSON keys, invalid types, non-finite numbers, unsafe paths, case aliases, shell syntax, missing validator references, and duplicate manifest identities fail closed.
One active target has at most one accepted governing contract; a superseding contract advances the same family and retains the exact target.
A pre-screen report is canonical, self-identifying, byte-equal to a current recomputation, and still states acceptance as not_granted when consumed.
An accepted JSON artifact retains a byte-identical proposal counterpart and is canonical unless its immutable pre-tooling hash is explicitly grandfathered.
The fixed transaction journal is canonical and recovery validates every backup identity before replacing a repository artifact.
Verification of one selected contract still validates the global manifest, supersession graph, and active-target uniqueness.
raises: No ordinary schema, path, manifest, proposal, pre-screen, acceptance, binding, validator, report, supersession, workflow, or transaction error crosses the CLI boundary.
Each classified failure produces a nonzero exit code and no success report.
KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, and other process-control exceptions are re-raised after transaction rollback and are never reclassified as ordinary failures.
requires: The accepted MH-C-WORKFLOW-001 document and schema-1 contract manifest are present and hash-current.
Every input path resolves within the repository with exact case and every registered artifact matches its manifest SHA-256.
Acceptance names one canonical proposed artifact, its current deterministic pre-screen report, its exact expected SHA-256, and an explicit authority.
